analysis.title: Tripadvisor Inc. (TRIP) Q3'26 Earnings Review: Leaning Into Experiences While Repositioning the Business
key_insights: Goldman reiterates Buy and a $11 12-month price target on TRIP (price $10.20, 7.8% upside) after updating its model for Q3'26 results and management commentary.

Q3'26 operating results came in below GS and Street (FactSet) expectations. Goldman cites slower Experiences growth, softer travel demand, persistent SEO headwinds and weaker marketing efficiency, particularly at the Tripadvisor point-of-sale business.

TRIP completed the sale of TheFork for about $685m of net cash proceeds. Debt reduction is now the key near-term capital allocation priority, with room left for future buybacks and strategic investment.
Management announced a restructuring of the Hotels & Other segment to simplify the business and move resources toward Experiences. It targets about $40m of annualized company-wide cost savings.
Strategy is sharpening around a Viator-led consumer flywheel in Experiences. B2B2C partnerships and third-party points of sale remain profitable growth channels, with B2B2C bookings up mid-teens YoY.

Management reiterated that AI is a long-term opportunity. Referral traffic and citations across AI platforms are rising, and conversion is about 5x average on Viator and about 2x on Tripadvisor, from a small base.
Hotels & Other revenue fell 23% YoY on lower traffic volumes amid SEO headwinds and an evolving search landscape.
Management noted continued macro softening, with weakness in long-haul travel corridors and geopolitical disruptions weighing on Experiences bookings and cancellation rates.

Estimates were cut. Q4'26 revenue goes to $308m (from $335m) and Adj. EBITDA to $12m (from $46m). 2027 revenue goes to $1.53bn (from $1.60bn) and Adj. EBITDA to $212m (from $266m). The largest cuts fall on Experiences EBITDA.

The price target is unchanged at $11 because higher cash from the TheFork sale offsets lower valuation multiples. The target blends 6.0x EV/GAAP EBITDA (from 8.0x) with an 8.0x EV/FCF-SBC (from 12.0x) modified DCF.

Near-term investor focus is on Experiences demand, stabilization of SEO-driven traffic, and margin pressure as the company changes its marketing spend. Longer term Goldman sees upside to profitability as Experiences scales and healthy FCF that can fund shareholder returns.

market_movers.rationale: Buy and $11 PT reiterated after a below-consensus Q3 and estimate cuts. The TheFork cash proceeds offset lower multiples. Goldman's scenario range is $6 downside, $11 base and $17 upside.

earnings_insights: TRIP Q3'26 reported total revenue $436m vs GS estimate $447m and FactSet consensus $448m, about 2% and 3% below. Experiences revenue was $285m vs GS $291m and consensus $293m. Hotels & Other revenue was $152m vs GS $155m and consensus $156m.

TRIP Q3'26 reported Adj. EBITDA $71m vs GS estimate $83m and FactSet consensus $86m, 15% and 17% below. Adj. EBITDA margin was 16% vs 19% for both estimates. Experiences Adj. EBITDA was $38m vs $46m for GS and consensus. Hotels & Other Adj. EBITDA was $33m vs GS $37m and consensus $35m.
TRIP Q3'26 reported GAAP EPS of $(2.70) vs GS estimate $0.19 and FactSet consensus $0.27. Reported gross margin was 91% vs 92% GS and 93% consensus.
GS revised estimates: Q4'26 revenue $308m (from $335m), Adj. EBITDA $12m (from $46m), GAAP EPS $(0.39) (from $(0.04)). Q4'26 Experiences Adj. EBITDA goes to about zero (from $20m).
GS revised FY2026 estimates: revenue $1,512m (from $1,549m), Adj. EBITDA $177m (from $223m), GAAP EPS $(3.12) (from $0.08).
GS revised FY2027 estimates: revenue $1.53bn (from $1.60bn), Adj. EBITDA $212m (from $266m), GAAP EPS $0.24 (from $0.42). Experiences Adj. EBITDA goes to $94m (from $127m).
GS revised FY2028 estimates: revenue $1,652m (from $1,721m), Adj. EBITDA $261m (from $310m), GAAP EPS $0.54 (from $0.66).
risk_factors: Competitive intensity, including Google iterating its travel advertising products and generative AI re-architecting the online travel funnel, which could change where travel ad budgets are spent.
Traffic acquisition costs: TRIP relies on performance marketing, so fluctuations in acquisition costs could hurt margins.
Broader macro and travel demand: normalization of consumer travel spend or widespread macro headwinds could pressure revenue growth.
Online penetration in the Experiences market: slower consumer adoption of online tours, travel and attractions would make Goldman's Experiences estimates too optimistic.
geopolitical: Management cited geopolitical disruptions and weakness across long-haul travel corridors weighing on Experiences bookings and cancellation rates.

tension_points.bull_case: Viator-led flywheel, B2B2C bookings up mid-teens YoY, AI-referred traffic converting at about 5x average on Viator, about $40m of cost savings and $685m of TheFork proceeds cutting debt. Goldman sees upside to profitability as Experiences scales.
tension_points.bear_case: Q3 revenue and Adj. EBITDA missed, Experiences growth decelerated, Hotels & Other revenue fell 23% on SEO headwinds, and Q4'26 Adj. EBITDA is cut to $12m from $46m.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A slower pace of consumer adoption in the online tours, travel and attractions market would likely make Goldman's Experiences estimates too optimistic.

theme_stances.key_argument: Goldman keeps Buy as TRIP shifts toward high-growth bookable marketplaces such as Viator and improves flexibility through the TheFork sale, despite near-term estimate cuts.
theme_stances.evidence: increasingly centering execution around a Viator-led consumer flywheel
